biography: José Mario Dias, born under the relentless Brazilian sun in São Paulo, discovered his passion for speed not on a karting track, but dodging delivery trucks on his beat-up bicycle as a kid. His father, a mechanic, fueled his obsession, sneaking him into the Interlagos paddock during race weekends. One such weekend, witnessing Emerson Fittipaldi's raw emotion after a near-miss, cemented José Mario's destiny. Lacking the funds for formal racing, he honed his skills in illegal street races, a dangerous school that taught him car control and nerve. He caught a break when a local Chevrolet team owner saw his potential, offering him a test drive that led to a contract. Dias enjoyed a brief period of success in the national touring car scene but has since struggled to adapt to newer cars and rising talent. Now in his mid-thirties, José Mario clings to his racing dream, aware that time is running out.
drivingStyle: José Mario is an aggressive, flamboyant driver, a product of his street racing origins. He attacks corners with a 'no-fear' attitude, often pushing the car beyond its limits in qualifying. His tire management suffers as a result, and he struggles to maintain a consistent pace throughout a race. He thrives under pressure, often making daring overtakes late in races, but his impulsive nature also leads to costly mistakes. He favors a late-braking, oversteer-inducing style, much to the chagrin of his engineers.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from an on-track collision that cost Esteves the championship. They trade barbs in the media and their races are always tense.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky racing socks, despite their questionable condition.
Before each race, he drinks a shot of strong Brazilian coffee and listens to a specific samba song for good luck.
Refuses to look at the weather forecast, believing it jinxes the race.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. Out there, you either win or you crash trying."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2015 Brazilian Touring Car Championship after a thrilling final-lap overtake at Interlagos.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2018 Stock Car Pro Series race at Curitiba, costing him a guaranteed victory and severely damaging his reputation.
